question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}(-\frac{9}{5{x}^{8}})=-\frac{9}{5}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}
$$

Now, we recall the graph of the function $y=\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14247879/assets/aeeed013b57f5fd8a554ca6613bf9e3fa9419ae2e0fd5920397c5b9cb0dd88fb.png)

From the graph, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}=\infty .
$$

Finally, the negative factor of $-\frac{9}{5}$ changes the sign of the limit. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
-\frac{9}{5}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}=-\infty .
$$
